newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - WALL STREET JOURNAL - AUG 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - WALL STREET JOURNAL - AUG 11.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal.

* United Parcel Service, whose talks to settle a strike with its Teamsters union broke down Saturday, faces a possible pilots' strike if a contract is not reached in talks set to resume in a few weeks.
* Digital Equipment is seeking to sell its computer-network equipment business.
* Bond prices tumbled, pulling stocks lower on Friday, as the Dow Industrials slid 156.78 to 8031.22.
* The Columbia/HCA dispute with the IRS over its use of stock options could have implications for other firms' pay plans.
* Liggett's tobacco pact was rejected by a federal judge.
* U.S. firms still view Southeast Asia as a sound long-term investment, despite the Thai currency crisis.
* Bond-rating firm Fitch is in talks to sell a majority stake to France's Fimalac.
* Coca-Cola said its third-quarter earnings would be weaker than expected.
* TIAA-CREF plans to tap into a number of new markets now that it has been stripped of its tax-exempt status by Washington.
* USF&G said it agreed to buy Titan Holdings.
* EDS's stock dropped 14.0 percent as investors reacted to disappointing earnings.
* Waste Management said its new CEO's pay package closely aligns his interests with those of shareholders, although he could reap a huge payout if the company falters.
* BellSouth led a group that won a wireless telephone license in northeastern Brazil.
* Presidio Capital shareholders are fighting over the pace of asset sales and over steps taken by Wexford Management's Charles Davidson to assume ownership of the company's remaining assets.
* The bond market could continue to fall if this week's reports on retail sales or inflation show troubling news.
